question: How much did JPMorgan return to shareholders through dividends and buybacks, and what happened to the share count and EPS?

answer.summary: JPMorgan returned $23.29B to shareholders in FY2023 through dividends and buybacks, up 39.2% YoY from $16.72B in FY2022 [F13545]. Dividends were essentially flat at $13.46B (-0.7% YoY) [F00404], while share repurchases drove the increase at $9.82B, up 210.7% YoY from $3.16B [F00401]. Diluted EPS rose 34.2% YoY to $16.23 in FY2023 [F00090], with basic EPS at $16.25 (+34.3% YoY) [F00087]. The share count declined modestly: diluted weighted average shares fell 0.9% to 2,943,100,000 [F00096], and basic shares fell 0.9% to 2,938,600,000 [F00093]. The basic share component accounted for 99.8% of the diluted share total [F00093].
drivers: Share repurchases were the driver of the +39.2% increase in total shareholder returns, up 210.7% YoY to $9.82B [F00401], while dividends offset slightly at -0.7% YoY to $13.46B [F00404].
EPS growth of 34.2% YoY to $16.23 coincides with the 0.9% reduction in diluted share count to 2,943,100,000 [F00090][F00096].
The basic share component was the largest contributor to the diluted share count change, accounting for 99.8% of the total [F00093].
risks_and_red_flags: FY2022 diluted weighted average shares outstanding [F00097] is marked CHECK-FAILED and should be verified.
Operating cash flow dropped 87.9% YoY in FY2023 to $12.97B from $107.12B in FY2022 [F00341], a sharp inflection that coincides with the year of elevated buybacks.

Buyback activity is discretionary and volatile; FY2022 repurchases were only $3.16B before jumping to $9.82B in FY2023 [F00402][F00401].

outlook.actuals_view: FY2023 actuals show increased shareholder returns ($23.29B), rising EPS ($16.23 diluted), and a modestly declining share count (2,943,100,000 diluted).
